name: Positivism
summary: Positivism, in its political form, is Auguste Comte's programme of rebuilding society on scientific knowledge after the French Revolution. It holds that thought passes from theological to metaphysical to scientific stages, that sociologists and a new moral priesthood should guide society as a spiritual power, and that order and progress go together. It replaces individual rights with duties, rejects popular sovereignty and class conflict, and in its later form proposes a non-supernatural Religion of Humanity built on altruism.
scope: Comtean positivism as a social and political doctrine: Comte's Course of Positive Philosophy and especially his System of Positive Polity (and its summary, A General View of Positivism), plus its later movements such as Brazilian and proletarian positivism. Answers follow Comte's mature doctrine. Logical positivism (the Vienna Circle), which is a philosophy of science with no political programme, and general scientific or empirical method are excluded. Many answers are low-confidence inferences, since Comte did not address modern issues.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Comte rejected laissez-faire economics as a metaphysical doctrine and held that capitalists' activity must be guided by the spiritual power.

public-ownership.rationale: He held property to be social in nature but regulated by moral means, and kept private industrial leadership in place.

property-fundamental.rationale: Comte called property social in its nature and a public trust needing control, so it is not an absolute individual right.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Property and industry should be regulated, chiefly by moral pressure from the spiritual power rather than by law.

worker-ownership.rationale: He rejected communism's political solution and held that industry needs captains as well as workers.

strong-leader.rationale: Comte favoured a temporary popular dictatorship during the transition and praised Napoleon III's 1851 coup.

state-harmful.rationale: Comte held that order requires centralised government and that government is needed to counter fragmentation.

decide-locally.rationale: He favoured centralised order but also regional administrative divisions; no clear position on this question.

traditional-family.rationale: Comte made the family the basic unit of society, upheld indissoluble monogamy and placed women's main sphere in the home.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Comte tied women's affective role to biology and rejected modern claims of women's rights.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: He wanted a Western rather than purely national outlook but valued continuity of tradition; no clear position.

gradual-change.rationale: Order and progress, with reconstruction balanced against destruction, make social change orderly and cumulative.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: He envisaged a Western republic and an association of philosophers that is 'Occidental, not simply National'.

nation-first.rationale: The philosophers' association was to be 'Occidental, not simply National', and he sought to weaken national prejudice.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: His slogan was that science brings prevision and prevision brings action, though he held moral problems need moral solutions.

revolution-justified.rationale: He saw revolution as a transitional phase that leads to anarchy unless reconstruction follows, and wanted to end the revolutionary period.

experts-over-public.rationale: Comte rejected popular sovereignty and gave guiding authority to scientists and sociologists as a spiritual power.

central-planning.rationale: He kept private industrial leaders, though under moral guidance, and did not propose a planned economy.

tax-inheritance.rationale: He treated inheritance as supporting the proper use of property.

widespread-small-property.rationale: He accepted concentrated capital under industrial 'captains' whose use of wealth is morally regulated.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: He rejected communism and expected workers to accept their position as public functionaries.

one-party-rule.rationale: He called for a doctrine-led reorganisation, but spiritual power only counsels, so no state party is prescribed.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: He called for a republic of social sympathy but also courted Napoleon III and the Czar; he did not defend hereditary rule.

democracy-best.rationale: He opposed popular sovereignty and held that treating every citizen as competent on all social questions was an error.

direct-votes.rationale: He saw the claim that each citizen can decide every social question as a metaphysical error.

workers-councils.rationale: Workers' role is moral, as auxiliaries of the spiritual power, not political.

natural-rulers.rationale: He held that a trained priesthood of scientists and sociologists is suited to guide society.

political-violence-never.rationale: He thought the age of war and violent revolution was ending and that spiritual power only counsels; he still allowed force against the gravest crimes.

war-builds-character.rationale: Comte believed the era of war was over and the industrial age was peaceful.

separate-church-state.rationale: Separating spiritual from temporal power is central to his polity.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: He called theology obsolete and workers should abandon it.

military-superiority.rationale: He expected an end to war and opposed European domination of the globe.

ethnic-nation.rationale: He pictured a Western association above national prejudice and based membership of Humanity on sociology.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Positivism is the 'party of construction' that reconciles order and progress, and workers and capitalists have complementary functions.

equal-outcomes.rationale: He held that industry needs captains and workers in differing functions, and workers should not seek wealth or power.

civilizational-union.rationale: He proposed a Western republic of nations bound by a shared positive religion.

self-interest-moral.rationale: His ethics centre on altruism ('live for others') and subordinating self-love to social love.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The epigraph of his General View says man's only right is to do his duty.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: He saw industrial society as the positive stage and a basis for peace and progress.

restore-past-order.rationale: He aimed at a new positive order, borrowing but rejecting Maistre's royalism and Catholicism.

results-over-ideology.rationale: He prized scientific method but built a comprehensive doctrine and polity; adherents would be split.

direct-action.rationale: He wanted moral reorganisation by opinion and a spiritual power, not street action or elections.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Comte's law of three stages treats the scientific-industrial age as humanity's goal; he does not discuss foraging societies.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: He saw specialisation as fragmenting but wanted government and priesthood to coordinate it, not abolish it.

profit-exploitation.rationale: He rejected the communist critique and held that capitalists perform society's nutritive function.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: He supported a temporary popular dictatorship but not class rule or class dominance.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: He held that industrial society was ending the age of war.

harm-principle.rationale: He rejected liberal freedom of conscience and held that moral duty, not only harm, justifies social regulation.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Comte denied rights altogether, holding that people have only duties; that rejects group rights as much as individual ones, so the statement does not fit.

organic-representation.rationale: He made the family the basic social unit, and his order rests on functions, not parties; the fit is loose.

total-state.rationale: He separated spiritual from temporal power and wanted counsel, not command, from the spiritual power.

territorial-expansion.rationale: He opposed European domination and thought the age of war was over.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: His polity rests on spiritual guidance, not feudal oaths.

universal-morality.rationale: He grounded morality in Humanity and altruism, universal and scientifically studied, while subordinating intellect to feeling.

single-common-good.rationale: He held that the true principle of republicanism is all forces working together for the common good.

workplace-democracy.rationale: He rejected popular sovereignty and kept industrial command with capitalists as captains.

rule-by-example.rationale: True spiritual power gives counsel and never commands, and moral authority shapes opinion.

reason-over-faith.rationale: He held that the intellect should serve the heart and that affection is central, while rejecting supernatural faith.

class-collaboration.rationale: Industry needs captains and workers in cooperation, and positivism seeks to reconcile classes under moral guidance.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: He honoured past figures in a positivist calendar and commemoration of the dead.

private-courts-defense.rationale: He held that order requires centralised government and that force remains for the gravest crimes, so defence is not for private firms.

workers-nation.rationale: He saw the proletariat as natural allies in a Western, not national, movement.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Comte placed women's main sphere in the family and gave them a moral rather than political role, rejecting modern claims of equal public power.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Comte rejected class conflict and held that order rests on moral guidance from the spiritual power, so government is not mainly a tool of one class.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Comte held women to be morally superior but assigned them a domestic role and rejected equality of function, so he denied a systematic disadvantage needing correction.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Comte rejected laissez-faire economics and gave government and the spiritual power wider moral and social roles than defence, courts and property.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Comte replaces individual rights with duties and holds that functions and capacities form a natural hierarchy, so equal legal rights as such are not his principle.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Comte saw government as limited and provisional, and Marxist state theory is not his; no basis to say either way.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Comte explicitly rejects popular sovereignty and the doctrine of rights; legitimacy rests on competence and moral authority, not consent.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Comte held that positive science yields objective knowledge that the spiritual power uses to guide society, though his maxim that everything is relative complicates the picture.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Comte stressed altruism, social solidarity and cooperation, and sought to replace conflict with order and progress.

separated-powers.rationale: Comte's central institutional idea separates spiritual power (the priesthood) from temporal power (government and industry) so each checks the other.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Comte held that property is a social function with duties, and that the proletariat deserves moral and social attention from the priesthood and the rich.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Comte favoured a republican dictatorship with concentrated executive power and a weak assembly.

clerical-rule.rationale: Comte separated spiritual from temporal power, so the priesthood advises morally and does not rule.

recall-officials.rationale: Comte rejected popular sovereignty and the idea that voters command officials.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Comte held that scientifically educated sociologists should guide society as the spiritual power.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: The law of three stages ranks societies by how far they have advanced.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is about teaching gender equality, and the statement now asks only about sex education.

reviewHistory.rationale: Comte prescribed priestly encyclopedic education and a domestic role for women; adherents are split.

reviewHistory.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is about teaching gender equality, and the statement now asks only about sex education.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Positivism holds the theological stage is superseded by scientific knowledge.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Comte rejected popular sovereignty and the revolutionary politics of assemblies in favour of expert guidance.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Comte accepted temporary dictatorship and rejected freedom of conscience as a dogma in favour of order.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Comte rejected popular sovereignty and universal suffrage as the source of authority.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Comte held that property is a social function whose holders owe duties to society, guided by the priesthood.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Comte separated spiritual from temporal power so that neither dominates the other, which rules out placing the clergy under civil authority.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Positivism replaces the theological stage with a scientific one and rejects divine right.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Comte rejected class conflict and held that order and progress go together through moral and spiritual guidance.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Comte favored small republics and limits on state extension beyond natural territories, so claiming territory by nationality is rejected.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Comte's law of three stages makes intellectual development the prime mover of society, not economic conditions.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Comte placed women's main sphere in the family and rejected modern claims of women's rights.

moral-incentives.rationale: Comte's altruism and duties over rights call for living for others, supporting moral over material motives.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Positivism holds that reconstruction, not destruction, is needed, with order accompanying progress.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Comte opposed hereditary aristocracy but kept hereditary transmission of property; no clear position.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Comte taught history as the story of Humanity as a whole, with a calendar honoring figures across civilizations, rather than of one nation.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Comte replaced individual rights with duties and treated property as a social function, so owners have no right to refuse on any ground.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Comte rejected natural rights as a metaphysical doctrine and replaced them with duties, so a rights document would be opposed.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Positivism holds that individuals live for others and society through duties, so withdrawal is rejected, though Comte kept rulers separate from the spiritual power.

filial-duty.rationale: Comte made reverence for ancestors and the family the school of altruism, with duties of children to parents central to the positive family.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Comte held marriage to be indissoluble, urging perpetual widowhood, so divorce on demand runs against his polity.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its value turns on whether representatives must follow binding instructions, and the statement now asks only whether voters can recall them at any time.

reviewHistory.rationale: Comte rejected popular sovereignty and mandated representatives, placing guidance in a priesthood and a provisional executive.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Comte saw industrial society as ending conquest and war, so backing armed rebellion in other countries conflicts with his doctrine.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Comte replaced individual rights with duties and held that everyone owes service to Humanity, so a claim of no general duty to obey would be rejected.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Comte kept private property but held that it is a social function under moral control, and did not propose common ownership of the means of production.

religion-illusion.rationale: Mixed: Comte saw theological belief as a stage that will be outgrown, yet held that religion meets lasting needs and founded the Religion of Humanity to meet them.

socialized-care.rationale: Comte made the family the basic social unit and women's moral role in it central, so domestic care stays private.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Comte wanted small republics within a Western union but not common property; communal self-governing property is not his programme.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Positivism rests on established scientific and historical knowledge, so denying documented facts conflicts with its method.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Comte held the spiritual power should rule by persuasion, not force, and treated theology as outdated, so punishing blasphemy is rejected.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Comte held that the theological stage is superseded, so religious law is not a basis of legitimacy.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Comte rejected popular sovereignty and metaphysical rights, leaving decisions to the competent under the spiritual power's guidance.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Comte rejected class conflict and proposed moral unity under a spiritual power, not an oppression-based analysis.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Comte held that theology is a superseded stage of thought and placed authority in science and the priesthood of humanity, not God.

racial-franchise.rationale: Comte's Religion of Humanity is universal, with the unity of all peoples as its aim, so a racial limit on rights contradicts it.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: The Religion of Humanity rests on universal altruism and fellowship, so boycotting people for their religion contradicts it.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Comte rejected popular sovereignty and wanted society guided by scientific expertise and a spiritual power, not by ordinary citizens deciding public questions.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Comte replaces theology with a Religion of Humanity taught by a spiritual power kept separate from the state, so the state does not run an atheist education.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Order is half of the positivist motto and Comte wants social discipline upheld by moral and governmental authority, not dissolved.

vote-delegation.rationale: Positivism rejects popular sovereignty and the individual political right to vote, favouring duties and guidance by experts and the priesthood.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Comte held that women's role is moral influence in the home, with the family hierarchy preserved and marriage indissoluble.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Comte treated property as a social function and wealth as held for the benefit of society, so income should follow useful work.

culture-before-state.rationale: For Comte the spiritual power and moral reform of beliefs and opinions must precede and guide political action.

person-over-state.rationale: Comte replaces individual rights with duties and has individuals live for Humanity, so the person is subordinated to the social whole.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Comte's later Religion of Humanity answers a human need for feeling and worship in non-supernatural form.

future-generations.rationale: Comte's Humanity binds the living to the dead and to future generations, implying a duty to those yet to come.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Comte held that women's affective, moral qualities are central to social life and the Religion of Humanity.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Comte sought orderly reorganisation under spiritual authority and opposed revolutionary upheaval as a prolonged crisis.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Comte planned a fixed scientific blueprint for society, so no open experimentation with systems.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Comte grounded sociology in a universal human nature and the Religion of Humanity, and held that it develops only within natural laws.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Comte rejected popular sovereignty and the idea that election legitimates rule; legitimacy comes from serving social order and progress.

women-suffrage.rationale: Comte denied political rights as such and kept women to a moral, domestic role, so he opposed women's public office.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Comte held that theological thought is a superseded stage, so literal scripture is rejected.

national-church-status.rationale: Comte replaced established religion with the Religion of Humanity, so no church holds special status.

self-ownership.rationale: Comte replaces individual rights with duties and holds that no one has a right over themselves apart from social service.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Comte treats property as a social function carrying duties, so fairness is not settled by acquisition alone.

missingStatements.text: Society needs a shared secular faith, centred on humanity rather than God, to hold it together.
missingStatements.rationale: Comte's Religion of Humanity was meant to give positivist societies the cohesion traditional worship gave.

missingStatements.text: Women's proper sphere is the family rather than public power.
missingStatements.rationale: Comte placed women's main sphere in the family and rejected modern claims of women's rights.

notes: Mill separated the 'good Comte' of the Course from the 'bad Comte' of the Polity; this profile follows the Polity, which holds the political doctrine. Followers such as George Eliot and Harriet Martineau kept altruism and a humanity religion but rejected much of the system, and Brazilian republicans drew on its order-and-progress motto.
